title: Placebo-induced changes in fMRI in the anticipation and experience of pain
how_used: Key fMRI findings: placebo decreased activity in thalamus, insula, ACC; increased PFC during pain anticipation

title: Placebo and opioid analgesia -- imaging a shared neuronal network
how_used: PET evidence that rACC activates in both opioid and placebo analgesia; rACC-brainstem coupling

title: Placebo effects mediated by endogenous opioid activity on mu-opioid receptors
how_used: Direct neurochemical evidence: PET [11C]carfentanil showing mu-opioid receptor activation in DLPFC, rACC, anterior insula, nucleus accumbens during placebo; rACC activation correlated r=-0.87 with pain reduction

title: Activation of the opioidergic descending pain control system underlies placebo analgesia
how_used: Naloxone abolished rACC-PAG coupling in fMRI, linking cognitive expectation to brainstem opioid control; naloxone reduced behavioral placebo analgesia

title: The neuroscience of placebo effects: connecting context, learning and health
how_used: Comprehensive review: vmPFC, dlPFC, nucleus accumbens, anterior insula; opioids + dopamine as key mediators; context-learning-health framework

title: Meta-analysis of neural systems underlying placebo analgesia from individual participant fMRI data
how_used: Meta-analysis of 603 participants, 20 fMRI studies: consistent deactivation in mid/posterior insula, thalamus, habenula, mid-cingulate, SMA; DLPFC high heterogeneity

title: Mechanisms of placebo analgesia: A dual-process model informed by insights from cross-species comparisons
how_used: Dual-process model (explicit expectation vs conditioned learning); dlPFC TMS abolishes conditioned placebo; vmPFC for expectation-dependent relief

title: Nocebo hyperalgesia: how anxiety is turned into pain
how_used: Nocebo mechanism: negative expectation → anxiety → CCK activation → pain facilitation; CCK antagonist proglumide blocks nocebo
